children: , the social-media and AI giant, turned Muse's explosive early adoption into a real-world test of whether consumer AI can become a meaningful subscription business. Shares gained approximately 0.5% to $744.80 Tuesday.

Reuters cited Apptopia estimates showing 2.8 million Muse downloads during its first 12 days, giving Meta an unusually fast user-acquisition start. The harder part comes next: converting that attention into cash. Muse currently combines free access with $20 and $100 monthly plans, while Jefferies modeled a longer-term scenario of one billion users, a 3% paid-conversion rate and roughly $10.8 billion in annual revenue. That would translate into 30 million paying subscribers generating an average of about $360 each per year, or $30 per month.

That math sets a high bar. Meta would need more than mass adoption; it would need enough users choosing higher-priced plans, while also building merchant participation around autonomous AI transactions. The valuation picture adds another angle: at $744.80, the shares sit about 12.86% below GuruFocus' GF Value estimate of $854.73. In other words, the market is still pricing Meta below that intrinsic-value benchmark even as investors begin testing whether Muse can open another multibillion-dollar revenue engine.

title: Meta Gains as Muse Converts Downloads Into a Pricing Test
